standfirst: This issue covers Uber's company-wide ChatGPT Work rollout, a new OpenAI Decisions API, Agent Skills moving to a foundation and a few tools you can try.
digest: Uber is rolling ChatGPT Work out to more than 30,000 employees after a 1,000-person pilot, and OpenAI announced a Decisions API for fast, low-cost decisions inside apps. Anthropic donated the Agent Skills standard to the Agentic AI Foundation, and Claude Code 2.1.309 fixed several sandbox gaps.

For a consultant, the Uber story is the useful reference this week: a named company moving past engineering to company-wide use, which is the question clients ask when they plan a rollout. The Agent Skills news means skills built for one tool are less likely to be locked in, since more than 70 platforms support the standard.

If you want to try something, Matt Wolfe's short video on Claude's Motion and Dashboards features shows two things you can do from a prompt. Genoffice is a free office suite that lets Claude Code create real Word, Excel and PowerPoint files. Both are afternoon-sized.
Expect questions about ChatGPT ads. OpenAI published how its ad stack keeps ads separate from answers, which is the point retail and marketing clients will press on.

items.title: Uber rolls out ChatGPT Work to 30,000+ employees
items.summary: Uber's CTO and OpenAI's Greg Brockman discuss moving from a 1,000-person pilot to a company-wide rollout beyond engineering. Useful for rollout questions.

items.title: Three new Claude features to try: Motion, Dashboards and Haiku 5.5
items.summary: A short walkthrough of turning reports into animated explainers, building live dashboards from business data with a prompt, and using the cheaper Haiku 5.5 model.

items.title: Team tasks in ChatGPT run recurring work in the cloud
items.summary: A legal team's daily intake review set up as a shared recurring task that teammates can check and refine. Enterprise plans only.

items.title: ChatGPT's Chrome integration analyses multiple open tabs at once
items.summary: A hands-on demo of asking ChatGPT to compare several open tabs and pull out the useful points. Easy to try if you use Chrome.

items.title: OpenAI shopping agent demo turns a room photo into an order
items.summary: A fictional retailer's agent takes voice and photos, recommends products, previews the room and adjusts picks to a $250 budget. Good for retail client ideas.

items.title: Matt Wolfe's weekly recap covers six new models and Krea 3
items.summary: A weekly roundup on Krea 3 image editing, Gemini 4 Argon and Meta's Muse Wonder tests, new open-weight models and OpenAI updates. Good catch-up.

items.title: Five prompts tested on Google's new Gemini 4 Argon model
items.summary: A short hands-on test of five different uses of Google's new model. Save it for ideas you can copy into your own prompts.

items.title: OpenAI's Decisions API targets fast, low-cost application decisions
items.summary: A new OpenAI API for quick, focused, low-cost decisions inside apps. The listing gives little detail, so check before promising it to a client.

items.title: Anthropic donates Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation
items.summary: The standard for packaging know-how for agents is used by over 70 platforms, including ChatGPT and Copilot, so skills are not tied to Claude.

items.title: Claude Code 2.1.309 closes sandbox gaps on macOS and Linux
items.summary: Fixes sandboxed commands running shell startup files outside the sandbox and being able to change the MCP config. Update if your team relies on the sandbox.

items.title: A restaurant franchisee cuts cash reconciliation time 94% with ChatGPT Work
items.summary: An independent Schlotzsky's and Cinnabon franchisee cut menu repricing time by 95% and built a workflow that could free up $100K in cash flow.

items.title: Terminal X grades AI outputs against a 54-criterion rubric with GPT-6.1
items.summary: An evaluation agent that checks outputs against a fund's mandate and catches 25% more deviations. A pattern for any client needing automated quality checks.

items.title: Itaú is building generative AI for its entire customer base
items.summary: The Brazilian bank pairs a conversational interface called ia.i with a governance platform, IARA, in a heavily regulated sector. Useful for financial services clients.

sections.title: Tools and skills you can use

items.title: Anthropic's knowledge-work plugins add ready-made helpers to Claude Cowork
items.summary: An open-source set of plugins aimed at knowledge workers using Claude Cowork. Check the README for what each covers before recommending it.

items.title: Genoffice is a free AI office suite for Docs, Sheets and Slides
items.summary: Open-source editors with a built-in agent, plus a skill so Claude Code can create real .docx, .xlsx and .pptx files. Bring your own API key.

items.title: Onyx is an open-source AI chat platform that works with any model
items.summary: An open-source chat platform that works with any model. Worth a look for clients who do not want one vendor; setup likely needs an engineer.

items.title: Firecrawl feeds web data to AI agents for research tasks
items.summary: A tool that pulls web content into a form agents can use, handy for competitor and market research. Needs some technical setup.

items.title: CopilotKit's OpenBot gives AI coworkers their own browser, files and tools
items.summary: Open-source agents that each get their own computer, with every action checked beforehand and recorded afterwards. Shows how oversight can work; running it is technical.

items.title: A Claude Code user built a pizzeria its own ordering app
items.summary: Claude Code produced the app, backend functions and payments so regulars skip DoorDash's 30% fee, and a first paying customer is live.

items.title: How OpenAI built ChatGPT's ad stack to keep ads separate from answers
items.summary: OpenAI explains how its ad system reads conversational intent and keeps ads apart from answers. Useful background for retail and marketing clients asking about trust.

items.title: A designer's AI-built side project earned $130 in its first month
items.summary: A UI/UX designer of eight years built an affiliate site with AI; almost all traffic came from Reddit. A realistic picture of early earnings.
